newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX CRUDE STILL HAS LONGER TERM UPSIDE.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX CRUDE STILL HAS LONGER TERM UPSIDE.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* NYMEX crude can rally again today if $19.49 holds, while $19.25 is an important support level for the week as a whole.
* Gasoline looks technically oversold so expect some stabilisation at the current levels for today and tomorrow.

NYMEX crude and products futures are seen holding a steady to firmer tone today. Despite last week's breakdown of supports on the daily charts, weekly charts continue to point room for crude to move higher, analysts said.

Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report, "The weekly charts for both Brent and (NYMEX crude) show that the uptrends have not yet been negated. (NYMEX crude) for example can rally again today if $19.49 holds, while $19.25 is an important support level for the week as a whole".

Tom James analyst at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore backed this sentiment saying "With Iraq news and expectation already in the market I am now looking for the technicals to start helping this market hold some support".
"Short term RSI's are oversold and looking to grant some support at these levels," James added.
$19.49 support is from Friday's low trade while trendline support, stemming from June 20's $18.35 low and passing through July 25's low of $18.98, comes in at around $19.25 today on the weekly chart.

On the spot month continuation daily chart the market closed below short and medium term uptrend supports. But long term down trend support from the highs of Mid-May is still intact and together with long term uptrend support from the June 20 $18.35 trough puts a base in the market at around $19.40-45 today.
Support for unleaded gasoline comes in at around $61.99 on the line of uptrend support that reaches back to June 23s low of 55.64 cents on the spot month daily chart.
Analysts were looking for some consolidation around this level today though remained bearish in the longer term expecting the long term uptrend to be broken.
Tom James said "On Friday the market opened below key one-month uptrend trendline support at 64.40 and saw quick liquidation to close below main support at 61.99".
He said "The market looks technically oversold in the short term so expect some stabilisation at the current levels for today and tomorrow ahead of the API's".
In the medium term he said he remained bearish for gasoline as the market moved on to its second half heating oil focus.
